subject: mathematics
question_text: Let A = {1, 2, 3}. Find (i) |A|, (ii) |P(A)|, (iii) all the subsets of A and (iv) the power set of A.

mark_split.label: Count the elements and the subsets
List the subsets and write the power set

recall_prompt: Say how you would answer this — say how you get the two counts, and how you would order the list of subsets.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Count the elements and the subsets
steps.margin_note: First mark. Parts (i) and (ii) both sit here. State the rule |P(A)| = 2ⁿ before using it, so the 8 is seen to come from a rule and not from counting a list.
lines: (ii) A set with n elements has 2ⁿ subsets, so

recall.must_convey: That |A| = 3 and that |P(A)| = 2³ = 8 from the rule 2ⁿ.
accept: A has three elements so the power set has two cubed which is eight
the number of subsets is two to the power n
count the elements first then use two power n
two power three ante eight subsets vasthayi

steps.why: The count 8 is what the list in part (iii) is checked against. Writing the rule first means the two answers are produced independently and can disagree, which is how a missing subset is caught.
steps.memory_tip: Each element is either in a subset or out of it, so 2 choices per element gives 2ⁿ.
common_mistakes: Writing |P(A)| = 3² = 9 instead of 2³ = 8, with the base and the power swapped.
Giving |A| as the number of subsets rather than the number of elements.

steps.label: List the subsets and write the power set
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Parts (iii) and (iv) are the same eight objects named two ways: (iii) asks for the subsets themselves, (iv) asks for the one set that holds them as its elements. Write the list once and put braces around it for (iv).
lines: That is 1 + 3 + 3 + 1 = 8 subsets, which agrees with (ii).
(iv) The power set is the set whose elements are exactly those eight subsets.

recall.must_convey: That the eight subsets are listed, and that P(A) is the set holding those same eight subsets.
accept: empty set the three single element sets the three pairs and A itself
list them by size one three three one
the power set is the same list put inside braces
subsets anni rasi vaatini braces lo pedithe power set
eight subsets and the power set is the set of them

steps.why: Ordering the list by size makes the count 1 + 3 + 3 + 1 visible on the page, so the list can be checked against part (ii) without recounting. Part (iv) then costs one line, because the objects are already written.
steps.memory_tip: List by size: the empty set, then the singletons, then the pairs, then the whole set.
common_mistakes: Leaving out ∅, or leaving out A itself, which gives 7 subsets instead of 8.
Writing P(A) = {1, 2, 3} — dropping the inner braces makes it a set of numbers, not a set of sets.
Repeating the whole list twice for (iii) and (iv) instead of naming it once.
